title: Single-Operation Service Contracts (Nanocontracts)
pattern: Defining separate remote service contracts or API interfaces containing only a single operation for every possible variation of a functionality.
why_bad: This represents functional decomposition masked as service-oriented design. It leads to service contract explosion, duplicates boilerplates, increases client integration and testing costs, and dilutes the semantic clarity of the service boundary.
detection: Remote APIs or service contracts containing only one RPC or HTTP endpoint, especially when multiple such services share identical underlying state.
counterexample: Highly specialized, stateless serverless functions (like AWS Lambda) designed strictly for event-driven utility tasks (like image resizing).
source: *Juval Löwy - Righting Software (2019)*, Appendix B, "SERVICE CONTRACT DESIGN" (Service contracts with just one operation are a red flag, p. 411).
